string.text: Know the dangers of the dredger? It has a lot of gravitational anomalies, but they are no match for an experienced stalker, just remember to throw bolts everywhere. The harder part is the radiation, the place is like a god-damn chunk of raw uranium.

Occasionally, you don't have to dive into an anomaly to find an artefact. I once heard a story, how one was found in the middle of an anomaly field by pure chance. One stalker was changing his detector's accumulator. Moments after he turned it on, it beeped and an artefact flew practically straight into his hand. Lucky guy... that's the Zone for you - one day it punishes you, while on another it grants you gifts.

Most go to look in the poisonous swamp. It's full of gravitational anomalies, but they are easy to detect, the water's dislocated in odd ways there. The chemical ones are worse, since the place is full of them, there is practically no air to breathe and if you stumble the wrong way, you will find nothing, except for pure sulphuric acid burning through your armour.

There's an old power routing station, called Iron Forest... if you ever go there, you'll understand why its called that. Artefacts can be found there after Blowouts, along with some electric anomalies and radiation... the hardest part are the poltergeists - if they see you, you are going to be pelted with all sorts of stuff.

At the burned down village, on the hill. A lot of heat there, but, naturally, also a lot of fiery artefacts. Check the homes - they say that where flames are after the release, that's where the artefact is.

I bet there's probably a lot of them in the caves under the burned farm.... when I went to the hill with my detector in hand, it beeps like crazy. You can get in easily, through a fault in the ground. Getting out is the hard part... there are many anomalies there, a lot of them, most are either the Springboard or the Fruit Punch, and I saw one move through the fault, Comet I think. A real mosaic of anomalies, but I suppose the artefacts there are different too...

Been to the Circus? It's a large anomaly with jumping fires and comets circling, a spectacular show. Better watch it from a distance, though, as the centre is, literally, hell. There are some artefacts there, sure, but looking for them is a sure way to piss off the fire poltergeist occasionally floating around. Hell try to fry you if you come too close.

There's a place here, where the ground looks as if a knife cut into it. There are artefacts to be found there, yes, but everyone who goes there reports of strange occurrences... there is something there that hits your brain, so that you don't know what to do or even forget how to breathe...

If you're looking for gravitational artefacts, look around the Claw. It's easy to spot, the anomalies truly changed the landscape, part of the hill just disappeared and in the caves under the hill Snorks have moved in. Luckily, they seem to prefer staying inside.

There's a place at the Creek, where the earth boiled and rose up from beneath the water. We call it the Boiler, since it's cut up by cracks with incredible heat inside and steam beating out. It's easily recognizable by a steam cloud hovering over it. Make no mistake - it's not harmless. Every stalker worth their salt knows that it's at least as hot as steam coming from a pot of boiling water.
I found a nice place in my travels: a lot of artefacts, but also a lot of anomalies. At the bottom of the rift there is so much bubbling that even a mask won't protect your face from hurt.

The Ashes is at the old cemetery, near Kopachi. It's extremely dangerous, a lot of heat there and occasional zombies shamble around. Generally, this place is best left alone, although you can find artefacts there from time to time.

Artefacts were once found on the old parking. There are no vehicles there now, but from what I know, the radiation is not low - the Geiger pretty much screams near that place. Oh, and there are also electric anomalies there. A lot of them.

In the Rotten Grove, where trees were twisted by acid. Anyone who went there said that there are horrible amounts of vapour in the air and the gas obscures vision very badly. But if what they say is true, artefacts can be found there.
If you look for artefacts, acidic are best. And the best place to look for them - the Concrete Bathtub. Little competition there, most stay away because of the Jupiter nearby.

North of the Jupiter plant, where the road collapsed. We call it the Asphalt, since it sits where the pavement once was. Inside the gap, there's a lot of anomalies - boilers, mixed with gravitational ones... but it should give different kinds of artefacts, since it's a mix of two anomalies.

There's this small swamp, north of the cement factory, one still called "soft" by some. It turned into a horrible, smelly swamp, with lots of gas around. While it looks like water, don't be fooled - most of it is solid acid. You can find artefacts there, together with monsters.

Look around the old cement factory. It's full of anomalies, but well worth it - there might be easier places, but the competition there is obviously bigger. Plus, there's only tushkanos around, and even then only if you go basement crawling.

You should go have a look at the Pineoak. It's that odd thingie among the hills, beneath which a chemical anomaly has formed. We call it like that because some nerd determined that the bark is part pine, part oak. If you want to get an artefact there, though, you need good protection from chem burns... well, and some ammo. And attention. Dogs roam the area in packs.

Experienced stalkers say that some artefact can move outside the anomaly. It happens, your detector will notice it, you try to get it, but there's nothing there any more, the artefact's days are over. Chasing them is useless - the Zone itself decides who is worthy to get an artefact.
Pripyat's rich in artefacts, yet no one's looking for them. Everyone I know came here recently and are extremely cautious.
Who knows where to find them... little is known of Pripyat.
I would look around in underground tunnels, they say there's a lot of them there.

Little is known about these places, mostly Garik's stories. He says there's a place where the acid anomaly grew massive vines, the size of a ten-storey building. He might have been exaggerating a bit, but if he wasn't, I'd surely go and check the vines for artefacts.
In the Zone, man, in the Zone. Be optimistic.
Good question. If you find them, tell me, OK?
Where, when, how... remember: if you find a good source, keep your mouth shut.
Where can I find artefacts?
I already told you.
No, I do not know anything more than I already told you.
That's all I know. Ask others around here.
We are currently tracking down a group of bandits.
We're looking for those god-damn scumbags. Freedom my ass.
My goal is finding the mercenaries we've been trailing.
We are pursuing a Monolith squad.
We are eradicating mutants, this should make the area safer for the time being.
We're doing nothing.
Chasing local bandits.
Duty is camped out somewhere around here and are spying on us.
I am following some mercenaries. They must pay for their past sins.
We're gunning for those nut job Monolithians.
We're tracking mutants. Risky, but we must take that.
Yeah, nothing in general.
Cheers, brother.
Welcome.
Well, hello.
Whassup?
Oh, fresh meat.
Oh, stalker. What's up?
Hayushki.
Hey, man.
Oh, hi dude.
Hello.
Hello stalker.
Hello.
What do you need?
What do you want?
Speak.
Good morning, Major!
Good morning!
I'm listening, Comrade Major.
Hello!
Bro, help me!
Brother... save me... I'm dying...
Help me out, kid ... Gah, it hurts!
Uncle, drugs... give me some drugs...
Dude ... ohhh ... Dude, help me out!
Man... need first aid kit... now...
Stalker help ... give me first aid...
I'm wounded ... Help!
I need meds!
Medkit!
Need medical help!
Medkit! ...hurry!

Heard of the dredger, just east of Skadovsk? They say it lights up at night, a strange thing... even for the Zone. In general, no one is sure if they want to climb up there and see what it is. It might be something valuable, but you might get your ass capped... time'll show...

News are just sad. Good stalkers disappear one after another, and their bodies are left without a drop of blood! A damn flock of bloodsuckers, I tell you. If only we could find their hidey hole and fill them all with lead, without distinction! As it stands, it looks as if we should go to the crapper in pairs! So much for being a Loner...

Listen, you're the dude who exposed the doc on Skadovsk as a vampire? Hey, thanks man. Everyone thought all was clear as ice, that the mutants are the only true monsters... but, as it turned out, our fellow humans can be even worse. Homo homini lupus...

Well, the Chimera at the Creek is dead. Some stalker worked with Gaunt... he looked just like you... it was you, wasn't it? Well, you know the story first hand then. I'd just like to say thank you - the place is much safer without a superfluous man-eating mutant at large.

Not really news, and no real secret - Cardan, the technician, is almost perpetually drunk. They say, that when he came to the Skadovsk, he drank purely for decontamination and on rare occasions. Only later, when his friends were gone, did he begin to empty bottle after bottle. Looks like his good friends turned their backs on him...

Behold, a new world wonder - sober Cardan! He just stopped to drink at all! Skadovsk guys asked him where did he find a psychic to help him, but he just laughed, saying that a squirrel brought him an encrypted code: 62.

Noah's new enterprise. There's this local, Creek folklore, a stalker named Noah: experienced, skilled and absolutely batshit insane. His latest fixation is saving all stalkers from the apocalypse. He took an old barge and tries to build an "Ark"... so far it's more of a totem to his insanity. If you decide to have a look, remember - do not piss him off. If you don't do it, he's harmless.

Met Nimble? He's on Skadovsk now, a real maestro. He can get you almost anything, though lately, he limited himself to just guns and armour. But what guns and what armour! Experimental designs, custom made tools... and steep prices. But hey, exclusive goods get exclusive price tags!

Did you know that the Pilot plotted new routes between the Creek and Jupiter? Previously, we had to go through a long, uphill tract, dodging anomalies left and right, while now... it's a breeze, not a struggle, but a walk in the park, taking even less time than before! He did admit that he didn't actually find the route, instead, he got it from maps given to him by a stalker. He still asks for payment, but the price is not bloated any more.

Yes, everything is old. Take for instance the abandoned convoy at the bridge to the processing plant - everything's rusted, including the bridge... but you might still find some salvage there. If only there weren't so many mutants and anomalies there...

I've heard that the Sultan, a bastard, would like to see Beard under his thumb. Not only does his gang harass Skadovsk, he also decided to drive the stalkers out... the nerve! He said Beard and our stalker brethren will bow to him soon... I wouldn't want to see Sultan with this kind of power.

Crap, did you hear? Sultan, that bastard, screwed Beard over... How did he manage to do that, I do not know, but he put Beard out on the counter! How did it come to this? You turn around and Skadovsk becomes a bandit base!

Brother, did you hear about the Oasis? They say that a place exists, not easy to find let alone reach, where there is a pond that, if you enter, cures all wounds and diseases... everything! Heh, what a tale... Did you see the newbie stalkers coming here? Some look for Klondike artefacts, some out of curiosity, but most just scour the area looking for the Oasis. After all, it is rumoured that it is in these parts...

What has the Zone come to? Someone found the Oasis and took the artefact, its Heart! Now the area will disappear into another dimension, along with the stalkers, who will never get out of it...! Just joking, in reality, the lucky guy has a new artefact with him, or so the scientists in the bunker speculate.

Did you hear about Poplar? He and his friends recently found a new hole, which they gladly climbed into. Well, before they got too far inside, a controller went medieval on their brains. They'd be shambling corpses now, mumbling incoherently if it wasn't for a stalker who came with them. They say that before Poplar's team could be zombified, this stalker managed to kill the controller and save their brains!

Heard about the Kopachi village? When the first accident happened at the Chernobyl NPP, it was blanketed by radiation, enough to make the authorities decide that burying the entire village is the best course of action. Only radioactive mounds remain now. It was awful back then, but what's there nowadays? Nobody knows. Everybody avoids it, due to fear... now think, maybe Klondike artefacts are there?

Do you know that on Yanov there are only two stalkers, that can tell the coming of a blowout? One, the Chiropractor, our medic and the other - Zulus, a former Dutyer... at least until recently. When did Yanov stop being Dutyer? When Freedom stalkers appeared here, they didn't miss Duty's arrival. During a shoot-out, half of the stalkers from both sides lodged there, with more and more free stalkers coming. When Zulus felt the imminent blowout, the situation became dire - with nowhere to go, Duty and Freedom declared a cease fire and took refuge at Yanov. Then, Zulus left Duty and stayed in the tower near the station.

Yeah, many speak of strange happenings... you shouldn't believe everything, in this place, storytellers are dime a dozen. Strangely enough, recently several stalkers from Yanov all reported that they saw an UFO, a black disk five meters wide. Some say that it was more like an aircraft at first glance. Just remember, a former military pilot was among the witnesses, who said that he hasn't seen anything like it in his entire life.

I heard rumours that all kinds of hell are going down at the old cooling tower. We scanned the frequencies and we can hear bits and pieces of emergency broadcasts, cries for help, seems like some cannot escape the anomalies. When we ask for coordinates, there is silence. But the weirdest thing is how the requests sound... they are distorted in a way impossible to blame on simple interference.

Now here's some irony. Guys from Freedom got hold of the legendary founder of Duty, or at least his PDA. You know what? Apparently he tricked his men, said that command threw them into the Zone with no backup, and formed Duty! But in the Zone, no deeds go unaccounted for - this bastard soon got into a spatial bubble, all the way in. There... I was thinking of joining Duty, but now, they won't get another recruit.

A new Duty squad appeared, out of thin air! Here's a thought - a small group of Dutyers leaves Yanov, but returns three times larger. Do they clone themselves? Well, that might be true, since it's hard to tell them apart. I'm still trying to figure out how they distinguish one from another.

A new Freedom squad appeared, out of thin air! Here's a thought - a small group of Freedomers leaves Yanov, but returns almost three times as big! It's obvious that they reproduce somehow, although with Freedom anything is possible... I guess it's the grass, you plant it, let it take root and, bam, your own, home grown Freedomer.

Know Gaunt and his boys? They went through some bad stuff lately - Daniel disappeared, Crab's wounded... they went blue collar, settling for scientific jobs, measurements and all. Lucky guys. They have the smarts, I suppose, and a load of luck - they might even get official researcher IDs.

Know the stalker trio, Mityai, Bags and Bear? I hard they settled for a job for the scientists, measurements and all. God only knows what the job entails exactly, but it's only likely that those uni geniuses cooked something special up. I'm not worried about the guys - a breakthrough here, a breakthrough there and they might all end up going pro.

Ever heard of Spartacus and his boys? You won't find them on Skadovsk now - they're guarding the scientists. They know how to fight mutants right and aren't new at fighting off bandits. It's a good cause and deal - the eggheads needed some relief.

You might've seen the mercenaries who camped at the workshops substation. They aren't there any more, rumours say they left for the Jupiter, to bunker down and protect the scientists, just like the mercenaries that did it earlier, before they disappeared. I think it's a good trend - mercs come and go... after two or three more changes, we won't have them bothering us at the Creek any more.

People saw that the scientist bunker is now under the protection of Duty's valiant fighters... wonder what's their deal? Maybe they hope the eggheads will invent them a new gun in return, a tushkano repellent? Hmmm, now that's a mystery.

They say the scientist bunker is now under Freedom's protection... I wonder if the scientists are aware that their research might be pirated? Heh, I think there are obvious benefits to this deal - anyone wanting to attack the bunker would have to go through that smoke screen... and most will get lost, I bet.

Seen Jupiter, the radio device factory? Awful place. Fuck if anyone knows what was going on there. Sure, the anomalies are the same and the mutant count is identical to the rest of the Zone... but no one wants to go inside too much... we all have a gut feeling that not everything's right with that place.

Heh, "what's new" he asks. After your little hike through the tunnels underneath Jupiter, the news travelled lightning fast that someone got to the centre of the Zone. You can imagine the commotion, over a dozen people wanted to go immediately, but Nitro cooled them all down, saying that the bay doors are shut and there's no way to open them. Of course, some desperate guys popped up, wanting to blow up the door, but so far, they haven't figured out where to get enough dynamite or what to breathe when they go down there, for that matter.

Heard about Garik, that stalker who worked for the eggheads? He chose to leave their employ, ignoring the official pass they offered him... Free access to the Zone! No, he decided to go to Pripyat. We thought he'd die, like all the others who tried it before him, but no, he made it. Didn't turn out too bad for him in the end - he met the military there, got a pass and is now an official military stalker.

Well, Freedom and Duty fought again over some major cache... they say there was enough weapons in there for three infantry divisions. I've no idea who managed to stow away so many guns, but the battle could be heard all the way to Yanov, alarming everyone. Everyone kind of got out of their way and the end result... well, Freedom's in control now apparently. Too bad for Duty.

Well, Freedom and Duty fought again over some major cache... they say there was enough weapons in there for three infantry divisions. I've no idea who managed to stow away so many guns, but the battle could be heard all the way to Yanov, alarming everyone. Everyone kind of got out of their way and the end result... well, Duty's on duty, apparently. Too bad for Freedom.

This is recent news. A group of stalkers, investigating tunnels near the Jupiter, stumbled on something, or rather, someone. First, their guns were knocked out of their hands and then, all the junk around started flying at them. Generally, no one can explain what happened there, but they've lost two good men.

I've hard that north of the Jupiter, in the tunnels, some god-damn mutant was found. Tutsan sent a stalker to reconnoitre the area, turned out it was a burer den. You might wonder, "Why was"? That's cause this stalker killed off the burers. All alone... according to his description, he's every bit like you, except taller and always toting grenades.

The end of stalkers is coming... at the cement plant, those damn creatures just kept coming, even dragging off a stalker. There was at least a dozen of them, all big and scary, looking like bloodsuckers, except twice as big and much, much faster. Our only hope lies with Tutsan now, who knows how to deal with these monsters.

Did you hear about the marsh bloodsuckers, those that were sitting in the meadows? They are no more! They say that Tutsan did it, but it's not true, he hired stalkers. They say it was a squad of about ten people, that combed the marsh back and forth, forcing everything out and shooting it. Not even a frog remains...

Yeah, they say that the Chimera people saw was killed. Looks like mutant life gets complicated - beasts with stalker body counts in the tens are now getting killed off themselves. The hunter was experienced, with at least as many mutants killed as us both!

Heard what kind of people Freedom recruits? There's this guy, Flint, who kept weaving tales about his grandiose exploits, that turned out out to be a true SOB. Heh, even that name is an understatement - he threw his comrade into an anomaly just to get his stuff. And then even more truth surfaced, where he practically fed fellow hunters to a Chimera. Freedom fighters used to have a better attitude... I'd rather be alone, than have such "friends".

Well, not really new, but listen. There's this stalker, Noah, who's gone completely off his rocker. Just look at his barge - a large, rickety tower, easily visible from a distance. He was building it for nearly a week, like a damn gastarbeiter. And then the fun really started - he shoots pretty much anyone who comes close. As you can see, quite crazy.

Know the deal with Nimble? He's a naturally smart guy, getting us rare or custom made guns, damn hard to find elsewhere. No, really, tell me, where would you find a Vintorez that never jams and stays perfectly accurate? The guy's a fucking wizard.

There's the rumour of the embarrassment Sultan suffered. Looks like the godfather wanted to get Beard under his thumb, but bit off more than he could chew. Flapped his wings and went down, he did. He has no respect any more, and he will have to revise how he greets youngsters.

The word is that Sultan managed to circumvent Beard and get him under his thumb. I say, he has wads of cash and a great authority, but the real deal is that from now on, our law is in effect on Skadovsk. And you? Want to hide from the release - we open after you pay.

Man, heard of the Oasis? They say it's a place that heals all wounds and diseases... a real, living miracle. Here's another idea - ever noticed how people shut up about the Wish Granter lately, but are chattering about the Oasis? Maybe it's just an allegory, of someone full of desire?
Word is that the scientists got themselves an artefact straight from the Oasis! Here's the point - apparently, studying it can create an effective cure for cancer!

Nothing new, just the old... we all remember stories about the centre of the Zone. For instance, the Oasis, a place where strength and health come back to you instantaneously. It's all bullshit obviously, but nice to listen to, especially the speculations about its location. Ah, if such a place really existed, just imaging how many of our guys would live to see another day.

They say that the Oasis was actually found. I never would have thought that it exists, but no use arguing against the facts. Inside there was an artefact, now scientists are studying it. Perhaps, they will be able to create a device for rapid healing... soldiers would love it.

Kopachi! Not new to the Zone, but it's still a novelty for me. Just look at it - an entire village, all houses, buried all the way to the roofs. Legacy of eighty-six - radiation in every house, just like radios. Awful place.

Know the deal with Yanov, with bitter enemies living under one roof? That's Zulus' work. He used to be a Dutyer back then, especially sensitive to blowouts. We came to Yanov first, before other stalkers. There was no time to smoke anything - rivals barge in, brandishing guns. Last time I saw a situation like this was at the Garbage, over a year ago. Lots of kids died on both sides, due to stupid fear and stubbornness. Then, Zulus stood up and yelled "Blowout, people!". Well, we couldn't really live humans like us to die, just outside the door, even if they are Dutyers. So, from then onwards, we live together, comfortably, biding our time, sitting through emissions quietly, just short of hugging one another. Zulus left Duty, choosing to live as a hermit near Yanov.

I heard a joke recently. One dude told me - straight faced - that an UFO flew over Yanov. Some ideas does the Zone give, eh? As if poltergeists and controllers weren't enough... thank God that at least vodka doesn't try to control me. As they say, "Begone, foul demon, let the vodka stay pure"...

Heard of Kopachi? When the first Chernobyl accident took place at the NPP, it was horribly irradiated, enough to get it buried. Completely, from foundations to roofs, only radioactive mounds remain now. They say it was awful back then, but what's happening there now - no one knows, and no one wants to find out.

Not news, but maybe you haven't heard the story yet. We're here, getting comfy with Freedom, not because we want to, but because we have to. When we first came here, they attacked us outright. Despite the losses, we fought back valiantly. Just a little further, and we would have owned the anarchists. But, in the middle of the battle, Zulus felt a blowout incoming - his sense is impeccable in this matter, mind you - and with nowhere to go, we had to postpone the resolution with Freedom. I don't really understand Zulus' reasons for leaving Duty afterwards, though...

Recently, out intelligence reported that an unidentified flying object passed over Yanov recently. An UFO, basically. Just so we're clear - an UFO is not a saucer loaded with angry Martians. It's any flying object - from a piece of plywood to weather balloons - that the observer was unable to identify. Understand?

You're the one who gave Loki that PDA? Dude, it's a bomb. To think that the legendary Duty founder, general Tachenko, stupidly took his men in, broke the transmitter, axing their chances of pulling out, hammered together a fighting outfit and then, just like that, disappeared in a spatial bubble... well, that's just GREAT!

Saw the armed new outfit? Apparently, they are not reinforcements, the ideology didn't quite ravage their brains yet. They are well trained, so they're no amateur stalkers... God only knows.... hey, don't look at me, I don't buy the claim they're former Monolith, no, this is absolute bullshit.

Did you see our new fighters? Oh, so you found them, and got them yo join, yes? It's cool dude, only, they're a bit stiff... ah, nothing, give us six months, we'll loosen them up a bit, get to sing along and they'll fit just right in.

We have new arrivals on board, former Monolithans to boot! No newbies without training - real professionals! 'course, their brains still haven't quite fell back into place after the Monolith, but it's nothing our political instructor can't root out.

Word is, former Monolithans joined Freedom. Who knows... fact is, they have a new squad, but it didn't come from the outskirts of the Zone. I think they took them in just to spite, or maybe their brains are all messed up by the drugs. Just wondering, who else will join their ranks? Zombies? Or maybe a trio of burers?

Soon, this area will be brought up to spec - Duty has taken key positions in this area, we are firmly entrenched at Yanov and near the bunker, giving our scientists 24/7 security. It's time for Freedom to take their toys and leave the sandbox, there's no place for anarchists here.

I remember, you arranged for our dudes to protect the scientists? Here's an individual thank you. Also, have some good news - the scientists look out of the bunker and instead of fucking mercs, they see our men! That's some positive vibes there, man!

News? We stirred up a hornet's nest by finding Duty's secret store. Heh, heh, now we'll use it properly, as a home for Dutyer prisoners we take. Thanks for the tip, without your help, we would never have gained the upper hand!

Another victory for Duty! The anarchists grew bold and vain, barged straight into our secret store and thought they could get away with that... certainly not! We cornered them and put down every single one down, like mad tushkanos.

It's not a secret that Freedom has a lot of rogues on board, but lately, one of those Guevara-wannabes turned out to be quite the rat. This Freedom guy, calling himself Flint, was once known as Soroka. He came to the Creek under that pseudonym and nearly got a group of hunters killed by a chimera, just to grab their gear and come to Yanov. As a Freedomer, he threw his partner into an anomaly, just to get his artefact. Heh, that's Freedom for you...
Nothing specific.
In the Zone, wherever you are, there is always something new.
You ask again. And, again, I answer: no news.
What's new in the Zone?
Nothing new, or at least I do not know of it.
I'd tell you, but I heard of nothing interesting.
I've told you everything I know.

Hmm ... I think you should ask Glouchar, on the Skadovsk. He was looking for someone to help him with the case of missing stalkers. They go missing, then turn up completely drained of blood, we all think it's the bloodsuckers, but the frequency... seems like a stalker disappears every other day, definitely not a bloodsucker MOD. Glouchar even hired an experienced hunter to track down the monsters' lair.

Maybe you should ask Gaunt? There's a story there... a Chimera appeared in the Creek recently, started tearing things up. Then came Gaunt's group of stalkers and started tracking it down. Halfway, one of hunters was hired to find the bloodsucker nest. And so, when they actually found the beast, there were too few of them and a stalker named Soroka fucked up. I don't know what exactly happened there... they say that stalker ran away as soon as he saw the Chimera. Gaunt and his guys barely made it out alive, one's heavily wounded and is still in the infirmary. And so, they are in dire need of people, since the mutant is still at large.
Here's a simple deal: you want a nice cut? Go meet Sultan. He's the big guy around here, if a kid comes up clean, he'll find work for him.

If you're a good stalker, you can look for artefacts and then go to Beard, he's a reputable trader. He's the only one on Skadovsk who will pay you full price for artefacts, he has connections that allow him to safely get them to the borders and outside the Zone. Besides, he's a nice guy, helpful and might just offer you a lucrative job.

There's this trader at Skadovsk, Owl. Not the most pleasant type, constantly moaning about Beard undercutting his artefact trade. He can help you with cash. He's a slippery type, though, and ammo isn't the only thing in stock... He knows a lot of stuff, and what he doesn't know, he'll surely want to know. Either way, cash changes hands. If you want to see him, he's on the second deck, in the stern. He might work something out for you.

Go ask Vano, he's always hanging out near the bar in Yanov. He got into a feud with the bandits, indebted to them again, for the third time. Weird, he's an experienced stalker, he can pass through any anomaly with his eyes closed, but keeps getting in trouble. We told him repeatedly to just go, the Zone's a big place and he wouldn't be found. But he's too proud for it, refuses to flee... no one seems particularly eager to go and help him with the bandits, though.

There is a job... the bandits grew quite bold, they took Mityai, a stalker, hostage and demand ransom. Mityai was one of the first to come to Yanov, set up everything to help everyone escape a blowout, but now... it seems no one's willing to risk his neck for him. Freedom and Duty are too busy screwing each other over, while the rest... hell, even Mitya's friends can't agree on how to save him... If you want to help, go talk to Bear, he's at the station, near the bar.

Nitro, the Yanov tech, just asked who can get him some special materials. He's not only an ace gunsmith, but also a budding electronics expert. There's just one catch - he has nothing to practice on. All safe places have been long since scavenged and no one wants to risk his life just to get some stupid chips. Nitro mentioned that to anyone who gets him the stuff he wants, he will be in debt.

I heard that Uncle Yar was looking for a discrete stalker on Yanov, for some business. No one knows why wouldn't he just ask his Freedom buddies to help. If you're a good shot, you could go and ask him, maybe he can tell you what's the problem and how could you help.

You know, when a stalker needs cash, he can do two things: either look for artefacts and sell them to traders, for one third of their real value, or go to the scientists for work. They will always find a job for one of us, finding a rare artefact, delivering a mutant carcass... but most importantly, if they find you useful, they might give you an official Zone pass! Imagine, you can pass through military checkpoints with a full haul, and they will even give you more and salute! Paradise! So, next time you visit Yanov, look a little to the west, they just dropped a scientist bunker there. One stalker already works for them, but I think they'll find a task for you.

Depends on what you want to do. If you aren't a mutant lover, hunting's always a good job. Look in Yanov's basement,Tutsan has an office there and pays mutant exterminators well. Just remember not to rush to him with every pseudodog you put down. Tuts gives out tasks to kill specific monsters that harass stalkers or dwell in places where you can hide from a blowout.

Work? Frankly, I do not know... but if you want to have a chance to help Freedom, come see our leader at Yanov, Loki's in the south wing. Remember - if you believe in human progress, compassion and the values gifts of the Zone bring to us - you'll make the right choice.

No idea. But if you find something that can give us an edge in the fight against our enemies or the Zone, talk to the commander of the Duty expeditionary force, Colonel Shuga. He is a senior officer at the Yanov station, in the north wing. You can be sure that all civilians who contribute to Duty will be properly rewarded.

Guys like you love to drop by Skadovsk and go to Beard. See, it's normal to unload artefacts to him... but, hear me - it's a mistake, the deal's not fair. He keeps the best stuff for himself and does not share it with the more authoritarian people. Soon, he'll be beard-deep in shit, you dig?

If you want something specific, then go to Owl. He's the Skadovsk trader and will have all ya need - guns and information. If yer have interesting stuff in your pockets - docs, PDAs, whatever - drop by him and he'll buy them. And then there are special deals, ask him - when he wants something, he pays double.

Word is, there's this group of guys. Some call them shamans, others call them druids. They say these guys don't carry any electronics at all — trying to stay closer to nature and all that. They claim the Zone reacts more strongly to electronics and electromagnetic radiation... and it sics mutants on you. According to them, the Zone is a living organism. They say you shouldn't poke it with sensors — a "pure" person can survive without all those extra gadgets. Though the hypocrites still carry assault rifles. You'd think they'd try using teeth and claws instead. On the other hand, they don't seem to die any more often than we do. Maybe they're onto something. They usually enter from the Belarusian side, though. It'd be nice to run into them... just to check how many artifacts they've got in their pockets.

Anyone here know about the classified labs deep in the Zone? Supposedly, they're still operational. Yeah, yeah, I know. It's a mystery how anyone could survive there without supplies or power. Makes you wonder — maybe it's not humans working there? I talked to this guy once. He never saw the labs himself, but he picked up some weird transmissions on a scanner near Yantar. They were talking about some facility. Another guy swore to the first one that he once ran into a figure in a suit like a stalker's, but way more advanced. And this translucent figure told him to beat it. "Don't interfere," it said, "we're working here." The guy nearly shat himself, obviously! Who's ever seen anything like that? Then again, it supposedly happened near the Radar. You know how it is. Probably a bunch of bull... but then again, mutations can be anything, right? Maybe they aren't even people anymore, but some kind of energy entities? Huh? Hey, quit laughing!

That Jupiter plant is a bad place. Gloomy as hell, and word is something nasty moved in there. Sometimes you can hear it screaming from deep inside the factory, other times it's quiet, but nobody's brave enough to check. This stalker we called "Lead-foot" once gathered a crew to head into that cursed plant. Don't know what they were looking for, but there were rumors of a massive tunnel network or even secret labs underneath — and you know how information brokers love that stuff. The expedition was doomed from the start. They kept ending up with an odd number of people, then someone named Sedoy blurted out that it was his last trip — and he was right, he never came back, even though they hadn't even reached the gates yet. They had to scrap the first attempt. Then someone's gun would jam at the worst moment... it was like the Zone was warning them to stay away from her secrets. But Lead-foot wouldn't listen. Five tough guys went in that day, and they all vanished. Not a single word, not a single trace. So take my advice, friend — don't go poking around there.

Zaton is just one giant swamp. But even here, there are places where an experienced stalker wouldn't set foot. The soil is soft — mutants have dug countless tunnels through it, and the ground collapses all the time. One minute you're walking along, minding your own business, and the next — bam! You don't even have time to react before you're swallowed by the earth. You're lucky if you fall into a cave; usually, people just vanish and nobody can find the body or the gear. A friend of mine died like that near the Emerald resort. All they found was his rifle and a patch of fresh earth, dug out like a neat grave — terrifying. If I hadn't seen it myself, I'd never believe it. No holes nearby, no burrows, nothing. Makes you wonder: is it just the swampy ground, an anomaly, or some kind of giant mutated mole or worm?

The Red Forest isn't far from here — every stalker knows the name. Don't go there. Don't even walk near it. The place is cursed. It's not just lone travelers who disappear; whole squads packed with top-tier gear have vanished without a trace. Only that old man, the Forester, knows how to live there, and honestly, I'm not even sure if he's still alive. No one's seen him in years. And was he even human? I doubt it. Even if you ignore the mysticism and the off-the-charts anomaly activity, a forest is a paradise for mutants. They've got plenty to eat there even without stalkers. No matter how much of a woodsman you are, without serious luck and prep, you won't survive the Red Forest.

Me and my partner had our eyes on this Research Institute for a long time. The place was eerily deserted. No animals, no mutants. But whoever went there either came back scared out of their wits, completely insane, or didn't come back at all. We decided to scout it quietly. Arrived before dawn, left the car in a ravine, and headed through the woods. My partner stayed below while I climbed a tree with a scoped rifle to get a better view. I saw the buildings — they didn't look completely abandoned. Most of the windows were intact, and the yards weren't as overgrown as you'd expect. It looked inhabited, yet there was total silence. Suddenly, I heard short bursts of gunfire from the right. I looked through the scope. On the roof of one building, some guy was pacing like a cornered rat, shooting wildly at nothing. I couldn't see what he was aiming at; he was alone. And then... it started. I saw it all. His rifle just flew out of his hands, like it grew wings! The guy screamed, pulled out a knife, and held it out. And then — I kid you not — another knife appeared in the air right in front of him. Just hovering there, blade pointed at him, held by nobody. What happened next... I shouldn't tell this at night. They carved that guy up for five minutes. Slow pokes and stabs... the poor bastard was covered in blood. Then, when he could barely stand, his knife was knocked away too. He was lifted into the air and twisted around like a rag doll. I've never seen anything like it. I was soaked in cold sweat in seconds. Then... No, I won't say more. Once I caught my breath, I scanned the area for another five minutes. My hands were shaking, the lens was fogged with sweat. Not a single creature! Nothing in regular or infrared. When I climbed down, my partner took one look at my face and didn't even ask what I saw. Back at the base, I didn't sober up for a week. When I finally came to, I asked around, but people just started looking at me like I was the one who'd lost his mind. So yeah, that's how it goes.

You hear it from the veterans sometimes — artifacts moving around outside of anomalies. Your detector starts pinging, you pull it out, and there's nothing there. That's a "wandering" artifact passing by. Chasing it is pointless; the Zone itself decides who gets a prize like that.

Let me tell you something — sleeping is almost impossible in this part of the Zone. I'm lucky, I can't sleep anyway, but folks have nightmares so bad they don't wake up in the morning. Heart failure, or they just go completely mental. Recently, there's been a rumor about a "cure." If you're desperate for sleep, find an old bucket... or a big pot... a metal basin, whatever. It has to be intact. You put it over your head and sleep like a baby. Yeah, laugh it up! I'll see how you're doing in a few days when you're collapsing from exhaustion. Smart-asses... Tell me then, why have the military been skulking around lately wearing those weird helmets? Yeah, for real! No sign of 'em for two years, and now they're everywhere. New helmets — guys found a body and checked it. There's a mesh inside made of thin copper wire, attached to the liner. Think about it — what's that gear for? I'm telling you, something's brewing. These aren't exactly prime anomaly grounds; there are better spots elsewhere. I think they're scouting paths. Setting up a beachhead. They're planning to break through to the Sarcophagus, mark my words. Something big is going to happen soon, and it'll hurt everyone. We just better be far away when the shit hits the fan.

We've got zombies all over the place, and you know why? Because the "Brain Scorcher" isn't the only psy-installation around. It's just the loudest and biggest, which ironically makes it the least dangerous. Some paths to Pripyat and the NPP are guarded by much stealthier units or relays. An experienced stalker only realizes he's in a psy-field a second before his brains melt. The range and power vary; sometimes your mind gets fried instantly even miles away from any known antenna. Stalkers find "rat paths," measuring the intensity and timing to slip through. But getting past a "mini-Scorcher" is only half the battle — on the other side, you'll find Monolith fanatics armed to the teeth, mutants, or just your standard deadly anomalies.

Flaunting your wealth and actually having it — two very different things. You think money comes easy here? Hell no! For free, you'll only get eaten by a mutant or shot by a stalker. You have to think. Think out there, and think even harder in here. Bullheaded thugs don't last long. It doesn't work if you're empty upstairs. Anyway, here's a story. Me and two guys, Sinyak and Tsepa (rest in peace), were cutting through a yard to save time. We see some "deer" — a rookie — walking along. We hid. He walked right past us, didn't notice a thing. Small guy, but dragging a heavy rucksack. Rifle slung in a way that he could pepper us in a second if we slipped up. Sinyak whispers to me, "Let's shake this pipsqueak down." I told him, "Shut it, idiot! Watch where he's taking that loot." Then the rookie just vanished — we didn't even see how. We waited. Twenty minutes later, he pops back out. While he was dusting himself off, Tsepa crept up and blew half his head off with a pistol. They started looting the body: the guy had a great vest and a fat wallet. I stepped away to take a leak — my share was guaranteed anyway. Suddenly, a huge blast! Turns out the "deer" wasn't that simple: he'd rigged his armor to blow if someone tried to strip it. I booked it out of there fast. I came back a month later. Not a bone left of Tsepa, Sinyak, or the rookie. Nothing. I figured out where he'd dove into the ruins and went in myself. Three empty rooms, nothing. Then I saw a pile of old bed frames in the corner. Why so many? I started digging. Underneath was a hatch! I opened it, shined my light... holy mother of God! I was in paradise! What was in there is my business, but I didn't come out empty-handed. If I'd been as reckless as those two, I'd be a corpse, or still running around broke like some of you lot.

So, my buddy told me this. He got woken up in the middle of the night by the brass — said there's a delivery for the lab. He's groggy, doesn't get it. They told him, "Did you drink too much of the government spirit? There's a fresh corpse on the table, dinner is served!" He goes to the table, and holy hell... he's seen plenty of Zone corpses: shredded, burned, boiled, mutants of all kinds, but this made his stomach turn. At first glance, it's almost human, but the head is all wrong: a huge, lumpy pumpkin. The body was skin and bones, like a famine victim. But he only saw that later; at first, it was just a mess of inside-out flesh and orange-red slime. Duty... "searching for anomalous objects," my ass! They'd turned him into a colander. They'd clearly stomped all over him with their combat boots too; just a lump of meat in black rags. He spent the whole night working on it. Turns out, it was that creature the locals call the "Illusionist" — black rags, psychic visions, head a meter wide. Funny thing is, folks thought its face was on its crown. It has a face, but it's tiny: eyes that don't open and a nose like a pin, but the mouth — huge, like a barn door. Probably walked with its head hanging low because it was too heavy to carry. And guess what these things eat? Mushrooms! Tiny mushrooms! Stalkers swear they squeeze the juice out of 'em. Gourmets, I swear. And you know what he had in a pouch on his belt? Dried brains. Controller brains!

We had this idiot join our group once. We're walking along, sit down for a five-minute break, and he immediately flops down to relax. When it's time to move, he's the last one to get his ass off the ground. Well, he "relaxed" too much. Fell behind, and a controller snatched his mind — snap! — just like that. Listen up, rookies. Any rustle, any suspicious breeze... even if a rabbit runs by (though rabbits here are terrifying), you've gotta be ready every second. Keep your mags and grenades handy, and your fire selector on auto. If you see something, dump half a mag; if something moves in the bushes, shoot first and ask questions never. This isn't boot camp; you won't get extra chores, you'll get eaten alive! And about controllers — that's a whole different story. If you shoot at a noise, hit the dirt immediately! Doesn't matter how. A controller needs to see you to lock on. While you're "sunning yourself" in the grass, listen hard — check if anything is creeping up. Swap your mag quietly, get a grenade ready. If it stays quiet, count to three and... run! Run as far as you can! Got it, squirts? Take care of yourselves every second — it's the only way to survive.

Here's what I'm thinking. I'm just wondering: what if everything here is just one big experiment on people? Maybe it's even little green men? Hey, it's as good a theory as any. I wonder: if this is a testing ground, what exactly are they testing? Checking which artifacts make us drool the most? Or maybe these are all just bombs? They've been scattered all over the world, taken to labs, bought up by rich folks... Man, that would be hilarious! I'd pay to see that! Some billionaire buys a weird trinket under the table, pays a fortune to brag to his friends, and then — BOOM! Oh, that'd be something! But honestly, who knows what's real. Only the folks who went past the Radar might know. But they can't tell us — they just drool and mumble. Maybe that's why they're drooling. Man, thinking too much makes me miserable.

Right... I remember someone asking me something yesterday. Oh, I remember now. People want to know why only our "eggheads" are crawling around the Zone while foreigners don't show their faces, even though there's enough material here for three thousand Nobel Prizes. Here's why. First off, why come here themselves when they can just give our guys a grant? Our guys will bring them everything they need on a silver platter. Secondly, they actually used to come here a lot. It's only in the last two years they've been scared off by a massive disaster. Now they just buy data and artifacts. They pay well, so plenty of loners and marauders work for 'em. Haven't you heard the story? The whole Zone was buzzing about it! It was a huge expedition. Thirty scientists from all over the world, top-tier minds. They were well-funded and packed with gear. They had a squad of special ops for protection and three local guides. They set off in armored BTRs. A week later, only twelve people came back in a wrecked BTR. They reached the fence near the Rotten Forest, but marauders were waiting for 'em. Those bastards didn't care where the people were coming from — they killed almost everyone. Only three made it out: two of our guides and one scientist. The scientist went completely insane from what he saw. Last I heard, he's in a psych ward writing a book. Our guys were okay, thanks to their experience. Though one vanished near the Radar and the other went back to the mainland. The rest? The Zone took 'em. Ever hear of Town-32? That's where they got hit. It was quiet at first. They were filming, measuring, poking anomalies. Then the madness started. Mass insanity. People started losing it. My buddy told me: one guy started clawing his own throat out, another bashed his head against a wall, and some just put a gun in their mouths. Then the mutants came. Those who were still sane barricaded themselves in a house. Can you imagine? Nighttime, mutants outside, and your friends going crazy one by one inside. By morning, those who could still think made a break for it. They drove straight through the anomalies to escape. Reached the Rotten Forest... but no one ever found the ones left behind. Word is, the number of controllers in that area skyrocketed after that. So yeah, nobody goes to Town-32 anymore, and you couldn't drag a foreigner into the Zone with a tractor.

So, here's what I wanted to say. When Duty took that "illusionist," I was right there! I happened to be in the area by accident. My car, my old Niva, blew a front tire: the bolts sheared off on a bump. I had no spares. I cursed for a bit, then thought I'd hike to the factory to find some parts. It was only a kilometer away — a thirty-minute round trip. I'd been there before. Suddenly, I see Duty! Not just a patrol, but like fifty of 'em! I thought, "Oh boy..." and dove into the bushes. If they'd seen me and started searching, I'd be toast. I lay in a ditch, barely breathing. Then the shooting started! I've only heard that kind of sustained fire once before — when they took the First Base. Anyway, I'm lying there, ears open. Guns are barking, then a massive explosion! Five minutes later, it goes quiet. I got bold, peeked through my binoculars. The Duty guys were limping out of the workshop, carrying a bunch of their dead and the Burer on a tarp... well, what was left of it. They vanished into a ravine, I heard the engines roar, and then they were gone. I waited, then went inside. Obviously, Duty doesn't leave much behind, but I was curious! Man, it was a mess. They'd shot the walls to pieces. Steel beams were lying everywhere, part of the roof had caved in. Shell casings were ankle-deep — it was a total warzone. Blood and guts everywhere. I didn't find much — just two full mags and a rifle pinned under a beam I couldn't move. I completely forgot about the tire bolts. I went back to the car, thought for a minute, took one bolt from each of the other wheels... and limped home. If I'd arrived thirty minutes earlier... yeah...

Yeah, I made it all the way to the edge of Pripyat back then. First thing I did was look for a high point to scout. Found a big boiler house with a tall chimney. Crept in quietly. Everything looked fine — dust on the floor, no tracks. I climbed into the furnace and started up the ladder inside the pipe. It was steady going; the soot had hardened and didn't even rub off. I peeked out from the top. Beautiful! Half the city right there in front of me. I pulled out my binoculars and started scanning. I was about to climb down when I realized I hadn't looked right under my nose. I leaned over the edge... and holy shit! I almost climbed right down into a Burer pacing the yard! Thank god he didn't see me. I couldn't shoot him — my AK was on my back and the pipe was too narrow to move. Мой Makarov was useless from fifty meters up. If I missed — and I would — I'd be dead. So I just watched. He was doing something weird. First, he was digging through a pile of trash with great enthusiasm. Then he froze, like he was listening. Then things got crazy. The trash pile started moving on its own. The Burer jumped back, stood tall, put his hands to his head in a weird way, and stuff started flying at him from all sides! Scrap metal, bricks, branches — he was buried under the pile. I thought, "That's it, he's done for." No way! Two seconds later, the pile just exploded outward. Pipes were flying so hard they got stuck in a concrete fence! The creature stood there for a bit, thinking, then turned and walked into a building. I took a minute to breathe. Then, I smelled smoke. Then it started getting hot. You've gotta be kidding me! Someone had started a fire at the bottom! A minute later, I couldn't breathe. I scrambled onto the rim of the pipe — no platform, just dangling my legs. The smoke was stinging my eyes, I was gasping for air... I had to go. Luckily, I always carried forty meters of rope for emergencies. I doubled it up, looped it over the rim, wrapped my scarf around my hands, and started sliding down, praying to every god I knew. One thought in my head: "Don't slip!" No harness, nothing, the rope was cutting into my palms. And of course, the rope was five meters short of the ground. I had to jump. Man, I hit the ground hard! Lucky I didn't break anything, but I was scraped up and my leg was killing me. I thought I'd torn a ligament. I ran out of there so fast I could've won an Olympic gold medal.

I couldn't believe my own eyes back then. There are beautiful girls, sure, but this one... she was perfection. Yeah, perfection. It felt like the world around her was black and white and blurry, and she was the only thing in color and sharp focus. The way she moved! I'd never seen anything like it. I had a lump in my throat. Why would she care about science? What was she doing in the Zone? Yeah, in the Zone. It was evening... there's a nine-story building near the bus station. I saw something in a first-floor window. I clicked off my safety, and then she walked out of the entrance. I wanted to rub my eyes — you never know what the Zone will throw at you. She walked up to me. I stood there like an idiot, staring... kept my rifle ready, though — habit. She noticed me, smiled, said hello. I was looking at her, not even hearing the words. She was in a blue jumpsuit, form-fitting. Her figure was... fantastic! It finally hit me that I wasn't listening — I was just standing there grinning like a moron. Turns out she was part of a research group. She asked if I could help her. Her! I'd have walked into a burner for her! She said she was studying Zone "endemics" — plants that only grow here. She said she'd ditched her guards because they wouldn't let her work freely, and came here alone. I believed her. I agreed to help, to bring her some samples. Two days later, I came back as agreed. I almost died five times gathering that stuff. I was walking back, thinking, "I'm going to see her again!" And nothing. I couldn't even find the building where I met her. Just like that. But man, she was something! It was like she was glowing from the inside.

The Zone was a shady place even before it became the "Zone" we know today. Right after the '86 accident. It was all top secret back then, but info leaked out, and the rumors were terrifying. People saw mutants near the power plant, ghosts in abandoned villages. Years later, a real nasty story happened. A group of crazy foreign tourists came to see the Zone. They wanted "extreme" thrills and apocalyptic exoticism. They bribed someone, and a whole Ikarus bus drove deep into the exclusion zone, not just around the edges. It vanished, along with its police escort. There was a huge scandal, and the Zone was permanently sealed off. They say when the first stalkers arrived, they found some very strange zombies... and they didn't sound like they were groaning in our language. Makes you think.

Back when stalkers were just starting to explore the Zone and find the first artifacts, scientists were already trying to cobble together the first protective suits and "anomaly detectors." Every new device cost someone's life or health. They'd drag a half-dead stalker to the scientists, they'd patch him up, and then grill him: "Where'd you get that wound? From what?" They'd take notes and add a new layer of protection to the suits or add new sensors. Trial and error is the hardest way, but the most effective. It wasn't easy for the pioneers to map out the paths, not like now. Today, you put on a decent suit, keep your gun ready, and you'll stay in one piece.

So, we're heading into that hangar. Dust everywhere, cobwebs all the way to the ceiling. Detectors are acting crazy, saying there's no one around, not even us. we started taking positions along the perimeter: Sanyok in front, we're covering him... and then — CLANG! There were these massive, rusty iron beams under the ceiling; one just snaps and falls! How Sanyok dodged it, he doesn't know, but that thing slammed into the exact spot where he was standing. He rolled away and, without even getting up, started blasting! The rest of us panicked like idiots and started shooting at shadows. Sanyok starts screaming about a creature in the corner. I look — I don't see a thing. It wasn't an operation, it was a total clusterfuck. We started prowling the ruins, moving carefully so we didn't end up under another beam. It was insane; people were seeing things and dumping half-mags into empty air. Two guys got it bad: one was walking on a flat floor and suddenly fell into a pit, the other got slammed by a falling door. We were pissed — it was obvious some creature was messing with us! We turned on our psy-protection, tossed gas grenades into every corner, and waited with our fingers on the triggers. We waited and waited... Turns out, the thing was flying, or something. While we were playing fools down below, she was sitting quietly under the roof, laughing at us. We realized too late. The bitch loosened a few more beams — half the roof collapsed right on us. Four guys crushed instantly. That's when we got her! Sanyok heard a rustle above and instinctively fired a burst — a hell of a reflex! The screaming! We jumped up and gave her everything we had. The creature fell from the ceiling, wailing so loud my ears rang. We really let her have it: some used rifle butts, some just kicked her. Sanyok pulled out a knife to really gut the thing. The commander had a hard time pulling us off, otherwise there'd be nothing left of that bitch to scrape off the floor.

They say people have seen new creatures — swamp dwellers. They look like bloodsuckers, but worse. Always skulking in the thickets, watching, and then — bam! — they've got someone's corpse in their claws. Terrifying. What's worse is they used to only be in the Marshes, but now they're appearing in other territories. The rumors about bloodsuckers near the border might be true. But what's that got to do with the Zone growing larger?

Deep in the Zone, there are secret labs, and they're still operational. It's strange how anyone could survive after all this time without supplies or power. Are they even human? What if they're aliens, beings of cold, ruthless intellect? Once near Yantar, a guy picked up radio chatter about a lab. The transmissions were so eerie he switched off his radio immediately. He was just too scared. Another guy near the Radar once met a translucent figure in a suit even better than a stalker's. This "ghost" told him: "Go away. We're working. You're interfering." Maybe the Zone really did turn those people into pure energy?

The first Blowout was a long time ago, right when the Zone first appeared. Back then, the military charged in headfirst — word is they wanted to deliver a tactical nuke and blow the whole place to hell. Но as soon as the vehicles and soldiers pushed deep into the Zone, a blast hit so hard it tossed tanks into the air. So many people died. I actually feel for those poor bastards: the ones who survived were just abandoned right there in the center. They were calling for help over the radio for a long time... but the generals were too chicken to send a second wave. They kept calling for days until they just faded away. Can you imagine what it's like — surrounded by anomalies and without protection?

I don't like those words — "latest news." Try using them less, unless you want that news to be your last. Even though the mutants around here aren't that scary, something happened the other day. This stalker limps in — white as a sheet, hands shaking. He starts confessing for some reason. Here's the deal: he and his friend were running from poltergeists when they ran into a pack of tushkanos. The guy snapped, some crazy reflex kicked in, and he accidentally mowed down his friend with a burst. He bolted, obviously, and the tushkanos swarmed the body — why hunt for meat when it's served up fresh? Well, after two bottles of vodka, his conscience caught up with him. He started wailing so the whole Garbage could hear: "Igoryok! You gave me your last medkit, and I killed you like a dog!" He wailed for a while, then hanged himself with his belt that night. People do some dark things when the Zone gets to them.

Word is, someone dug up old Soviet caches at the Garbage. After the Chernobyl accident, whole convoys of equipment and gear were dumped there. They thought it was all radioactive and useless. That's what they thought back then, but now? Nobody gives a damn! Who considers that level of radiation dangerous anymore? Anyway, they say a real gold rush has started there. Stalkers from all over the Zone are flocking there to dig. It's a shame so little of that loot makes it all the way up here.

When the first accident hit the Chernobyl NPP, the radiation was so bad they decided to bury the whole village. Now, only radioactive mounds remain where houses once stood. Folks say it was a creepy spot even then, but what's going on there now — nobody really knows. Everyone avoids it like the plague. But what if they're wrong to stay away? What if the artifact Klondike is hidden right there?
